title: Similar Triangles and the Triangle Proportionality Theorem
seo_title: Geometry Similar Triangles and Proportionality Worksheets (TEKS G.7B, G.8A)
standard_text: G.7B apply the Angle-Angle criterion to verify similar triangles and apply the proportionality of the corresponding sides to solve problems; G.8A prove theorems about similar triangles, including the Triangle Proportionality theorem, and apply these theorems to solve problems
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.7B and G.8A: AA similarity, nested triangles, the Triangle Proportionality Theorem and indirect measurement. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Two congruent angles make triangles similar.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • AA: two pairs of congruent angles make triangles similar.
  • Similar triangles have proportional corresponding sides.
  • Triangle Proportionality Theorem: a line parallel to one side divides the other two sides proportionally.
  • Use shadows or mirrors to measure tall things.

Examples

Example

A 6 ft person casts a 4 ft shadow; a tree casts 18 ft

6/4 = h/18

Answer: 27 ft

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Matching non-corresponding sidesMatch by the angles.
Using a part instead of the whole sideNested triangles use whole sides.
Upside-down proportionsKeep the same order in both ratios.

items.q: In △ABC, AB = 3, AC = 5 and m∠A = 105°. In △DEF, DE = 9, DF = 17 and m∠D = 105°. Are the triangles similar?
items.e: The angles match, but 9 ÷ 3 ≠ 17 ÷ 5, so the sides are not proportional. No.

items.q: △ABC has angles of 40° and 42°. △DEF has angles of 42° and 98°. Are the triangles similar?
items.e: The third angle of △ABC is 98°, so both triangles have angles 40°, 42° and 98°. Two pairs of congruent angles: Yes, by AA similarity.

items.q: A 4 ft post casts a 3 ft shadow. A nearby tower casts a 30 ft shadow. How tall is the tower?
items.e: Heights and shadows are proportional: 4/3 = h/30, so h = 40 ft.

items.q: Jayden puts a mirror on the ground 2 ft from himself and 18 ft from a wall. His eyes are 5 ft above the ground, and he sees the top of a sign on the wall in the mirror. How high is the top of the sign?
items.e: The angles at the mirror are equal, so the triangles are similar: 5/2 = h/18, h = 45 ft.
